full_caption: Nikolai Prendergast, Appellant, v. Lucian Dunmoor, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Nikolai Prendergast, the association governing the Saltmarsh subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Lucian Dunmoor from maintaining a detached structure at 723 Harper's Cut, Harrowgate, KS in violation of Article V of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The business judgment rule shields the board's maintenance and budgeting decisions from judicial second-guessing where the board acted within its authority, on an informed basis, and in the honest belief that the action served the association.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 22 comparable violations over a period of 15 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The association's architectural review committee denied the application by letter dated April 6, 2011. The declaration requires that denials state the specific ground relied upon; the letter recited only that the proposal was 'not in harmony with the community.'

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Covenants are construed in favor of the free use of land. Ambiguity in a restriction is resolved against the party seeking to enforce it, and a restriction will not be extended by implication to conduct not fairly within its terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article VIII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The defense of changed conditions requires a showing that the character of the neighborhood has so altered that the original purpose of the restriction can no longer be achieved. Isolated violations elsewhere in the subdivision do not meet that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Article V prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Lucian Dunmoor measures 300 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Fines totaling $100 were imposed without the hearing required by the bylaws. A fine imposed in disregard of the association's own procedural requirements is void, without regard to the merits of the underlying violation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW PROCEDURE
sections.text: No structure, addition, fence, or exterior alteration shall be commenced until plans have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee. The Committee shall act within 90 days of a complete submission; failure to act within that period constitutes approval. Any denial shall be in writing and shall identify the specific provision of the Declaration or published guideline on which it rests. Approval may not be withheld on grounds of personal taste alone.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.
